bibliographic.title: Mapping the Ethics of Generative AI: A Comprehensive Scoping Review
bibliographic.citation_apa: Hagendorff, T. (2024). Mapping the ethics of generative AI: A comprehensive scoping review. Minds and Machines, 34, 39. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11023-024-09694-w

methodology.sample_description: Literature on the ethics of generative artificial intelligence, including especially large language models and text-to-image models
methodology.technology_context: Generative AI comprising large, foundation, or frontier models capable of text-to-text, text-to-image, image-to-text, text-to-code, text-to-audio, text-to-video, or text-to-3D; includes LLMs and text-to-image models

eligibility.decision_rationale: Scoping review that maps 378 normative ethical issues across 19 topic areas for generative AI including LLMs, covering fairness, safety, privacy, interaction risks, security, and alignment. Highly relevant as foundational ethical and governance framing for generative AI/LLMs, but the provided text does not focus on conversational governance, operational controls, or regulated high-stakes deployment contexts as primary objects of study.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial introduction (pages 1-2) are available; full search strategy, inclusion criteria, screening process, and complete topic taxonomy cannot be verified from the excerpt.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal based on abstract and partial introduction only. Objective and scoping-review design appear appropriate for mapping normative discourse, but detailed reporting of search, selection, and synthesis procedures is not visible in the provided text.

cerqual.explanation: The study presents a coherent scoping-review aim and reports a structured taxonomy of 378 normative issues in 19 areas. Confidence is moderated because the excerpt lacks full methodological detail and because relevance to conversational governance in regulated environments is indirect rather than central.

coding.subtheme: Normative taxonomy and prevalence mapping of ethical issues

synthesis.main_claim: A scoping review synthesizes recent ethical discourse on generative artificial intelligence and maps 378 normative issues across 19 topic areas, ranking them by prevalence in the literature.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a comprehensive taxonomy and overview of ethical debates surrounding generative AI, especially LLMs and text-to-image models, intended for scholars, practitioners, and policymakers.
synthesis.limitations: The abstract states the authors discuss imbalances in the literature and explore unsubstantiated risk scenarios; full study limitations are unclear from the provided excerpt.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence for normative issues, ethical taxonomies, and governance-related concepts in generative AI and LLMs. Not primary evidence for conversational governance mechanisms, operational guardrails, audit/logging practices, or regulated-domain deployment.
